the use of communication tools as a means of innovation in the teaching-learning process.
the use that the student population makes of the Internet and the development of critical and reflexive skills as a consequence of that use.
the use of the Internet by university students as an innovative methodology in order to reflect upon and improve their learning process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of ICTs in the classroom, and the use of the Internet as a space for reflection, has allowed the development of a critical and reflexive attitude towards the use and abuse of the same in the university context, as well as the creation of a democratic, deliberative and reflective citizenship.

we are not only using technology for technology sake, but we are also using the new technology to develop the students' capacity of critical thinking, and the development of a critical and reflexive attitude towards the use of the new technologies.

we have been able to demonstrate how the use of ICT and the Internet, in the classroom and the use of the 'debate' and 'essay' as methodological tools, have allowed us to develop critical thinking and reflexive skills in our students.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the era of the Internet, the use of face to face conversations in the classroom and the use of personal life histories as methodological tools to reflect and innovate as a teacher, is more efficient in the formation of a democratic and critical citizenship than the use of technology and social networks.
